page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-90-lssd is a memory-optimized and storage-rich instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 45 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512 VNNI, and AVX512 BF16. System memory measures 720 GB, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is bundled as 3216 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across eight drives. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational throughput and memory performance. The multi-core stress-ng benchmark recorded 129,175.86, placing it in the top 25 percent, while Geekbench multi-core reached 19,780.0. The instance achieved top 10 percent scores on PassMark overall CPU (87,474.24), extended instructions (115,257.04), and encryption (100,477.67), alongside top-tier results in software compilation with Clang (60,820.0) and ray tracing (91,776.0). Uncached memory read bandwidth delivered 217.31 GB/sec, supporting Redis operations at 118.1 million operations per second and static web throughput of 53.81 GB/sec. Large uncached write bandwidth was average at 77.28 GB/sec, as were single-core metrics.

With substantial RAM density and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, this server offers efficient resource consolidation for I/O-heavy and memory-intensive applications. It is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching tiers, distributed data processing, Clang build farms, and heavy database operations. Systems requiring continuous GPU acceleration or balanced read-write memory streams should evaluate instances with dedicated accelerators or alternative memory bus layouts.

The instance features 720 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, and includes 3216 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across eight drives. It does not include discrete GPUs. Benchmarks highlight upper-tier multi-threaded execution, with PassMark CPU score reaching 87,474.24, Clang compilation scoring 60,820.0, and Redis throughput exceeding 118 million operations per second. Memory read bandwidth reaches 217.31 GB/sec for uncached blocks, though uncached write speeds are moderate at 77.28 GB/sec. This configuration provides a consolidated platform for memory-resident workloads, in-memory databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency transactional database environments.
